title: Microsoft Authenticator: Improved backup and restore experience for Android
summary: Microsoft Authenticator for Android will improve backup and restore with clearer setup guidance and support for passkeys starting mid-January 2027. Users must enable Google One backup and screen lock. Work/school accounts aren’t backed up, and backup works only in the Android personal profile. No admin action needed.
body:
[What and why]

We’re improving the backup and restore experience in Microsoft Authenticator for Android. When setting up Authenticator on a new device, users will receive guidance tailored to whether they still have access to their previous device. They will also receive guidance on using Authenticator passkeys for cross-device sign-in. This experience is already available on iOS.

To use backup and restore on a new Android device, users must enable Google One backup and screen lock.

[Rollout schedule]

- General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in mid-January 2027 and expected to complete in mid-January 2027[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

- Users of Microsoft Authenticator on AndroidPlatforms and services

- Microsoft Authenticator for AndroidWhat will happen

- When setting up Authenticator on a new Android device, users will see clearer guidance based on whether they still have access to their previous device.- Users will receive guidance for using Authenticator passkeys for cross-device sign-in.- Work or school accounts are not backed up. This is not changing.- Backup will continue to support TOTP credentials for Microsoft personal accounts and third-party accounts.- Users must enable Google One backup and screen lock to use this backup and restore experience.- Backup and restore is supported only when Microsoft Authenticator is installed in the Android personal profile. It is not supported when Authenticator is installed in an Android work profile.[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

Organizations may choose to inform users about the updated restore experience on Android devices.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
bodyHtml:
[What and why]

We’re improving the backup and restore experience in Microsoft Authenticator for Android. When setting up Authenticator on a new device, users will receive guidance tailored to whether they still have access to their previous device. They will also receive guidance on using Authenticator passkeys for cross-device sign-in. This experience is already available on iOS.

To use backup and restore on a new Android device, users must enable Google One backup and screen lock.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in mid-January 2027 and expected to complete in mid-January 2027

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of Microsoft Authenticator on Android

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Authenticator for Android

What will happen

  • When setting up Authenticator on a new Android device, users will see clearer guidance based on whether they still have access to their previous device.
  • Users will receive guidance for using Authenticator passkeys for cross-device sign-in.
  • Work or school accounts are not backed up. This is not changing.
  • Backup will continue to support TOTP credentials for Microsoft personal accounts and third-party accounts.
  • Users must enable Google One backup and screen lock to use this backup and restore experience.
  • Backup and restore is supported only when Microsoft Authenticator is installed in the Android personal profile. It is not supported when Authenticator is installed in an Android work profile.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

Organizations may choose to inform users about the updated restore experience on Android devices.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
